correctness.rationale: At φ_H=1/(2−a), a∈(0,1), ε>0, the coexistence equilibrium has Jacobian eigenvalues ±iω, V=(1−φ_H)(1−a)>0 and q=φ_H/ε>0. With X=u−1, Y=(v−V)/(εω), direct algebra yields X’=−ωY−qX²−ωXY−qX³, Y’=ωX+XY. Polar reduction R’=R²A(θ)+R³B(θ), θ’=ω+RC(θ)+R²D(θ), has zero average quadratic radial and linear angular terms. Exact trigonometric averages give radial normal form μ=<B>−<AC>/ω=−q/4 and phase frequency coefficient ν=<UC>−<C²>/ω=−(ω²+4q²+5q+1)/(24ω), where U is periodic primitive A/ω. Uniform normal-form remainders imply ρ²=2/(qt)+O(t^−3/2); angular residual O(ρ³) is integrable, so the lifted phase has a finite constant after ωt+(2ν/q)log t and the log coefficient is always negative. Near-identity transforms vanish in the tR² and phase limits. The transversality of real eigenvalue part at φ_H and μ<0 give the supercritical local Hopf direction, which is known and not claimed novel. Independent high-resolution Fourier quadrature of radial/phase means for three parameter pairs corroborates exact symbolic formulas; finite trajectory runs are not infinite proofs.
